title: Reuse native planning owners for checked task-sync successors
outcome: Factor transaction-local native reopen and planning transitions so a checked task-sync successor applies retained local construction identities without changing live authority or bypassing ordinary holds.
acceptance: Native reopen, revision, prerequisite and blocker transitions expose transaction-local cores while their ordinary public operations retain existing replay, authority, hold, lifecycle, graph and validation behavior.

A checked successor applies only within its opaque checked transaction and selected scope after local execution ends normally; native reopening creates fresh unclaimed Open generations and preserves older terminal runs, seals, evidence, original creation provenance and required-child accounting.

Every new native event, run and root-execution identity comes from the retained construction plan; the shared native event appender keeps canonical, relation, root-reference, feed and projection checks. Reopening orders ancestors before children, and no temporary hold deletion, generic skip flag, host proof or runtime authority transfer is introduced.

Focused native tests cover successful completed-run reopening/planning, active and unfinished-run refusal, stale basis/identity refusal, preservation of earlier completion evidence, ordinary hold refusal and SQL rollback. Deliver an author-checked exact patch/API package to the parent; the combined feature owns final integration validation.

completion.summary: Delivered shared transaction-local native reopen, revision, prerequisite and blocker cores for checked planning successors, preserving ordinary replay/authority/hold checks, retained construction identities and historical completion evidence.
